Russia and Ukraine agreed in Abu Dhabi to the war's largest prisoner exchange, more than 1,000 per side, but made no breakthrough on territory as the talks ended on 11 November.
US envoys Witkoff and Kushner arrived in Moscow on 12 November to meet Putin, and will brief Zelensky and European leaders in Dublin afterwards.
Russia struck Kyiv overnight on 12 November with a ballistic missile and 123 drones hours after the talks ended; the mayor said one person was killed and seven injured.
The US Justice Department charged three Iran-backed operatives, alleging one orchestrated a plot at RAF Fairford, a British base used by US bombers.
British police arrested a 41-year-old US Army member near Gloucester on suspicion of spying for Russia; officials say he served in a NATO corps headquarters.
France summoned Iran's ambassador over cyberattacks it blames on the Revolutionary Guard that disabled supermarket fridges; Iran denies any role.
Drones from Ukraine's attack on the Russian port of Ust-Luga strayed into Lithuanian and Estonian airspace; NATO jets were scrambled and Estonia asked Kyiv to explain.
Kyiv Post reported that EU ambassadors gave preliminary approval to sanctions on 145 Russia-linked targets, including 50 banks; foreign ministers are expected to adopt them on 16 November.
